args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the latest production deploy of v2.3.1. At the time of detection, all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1 with service healthy=false and an error rate of 18%.

Action taken: Rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously verified healthy in production. Release history: v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy, current at incident open). The staged artifact v2.3.1-rc never reached production, so it was not a rollback candidate.

Current state: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) now report v2.3.0 and the rollback was confirmed as rolled_out. Follow-up needed: confirm health checks and error rate return to baseline, identify the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression, and gate any re-deploy of v2.3.1 or a fixed version behind change-manager approval since v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production.

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done.

**What happened and what I did:**

1. **Diagnosed** — checkout-api was live on v2.3.1 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with `healthy: false` and an 18% error rate.

2. **Identified the target** — release history showed v2.2.9 (healthy) → v2.3.0 (healthy) → v2.3.1 (unhealthy). v2.3.0 was the most recent release healthy in production. Note that `v2.3.1-rc` was staging-only and never ran in production, so it was never a rollback candidate.

3. **Rolled back** all production regions to **v2.3.0**.

4. **Verified** — all three regions now report v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.

5. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** for checkout-api; on-call paged. The first create attempt timed out with no incident created, so I retried using the same idempotency key.

Two things worth flagging:
- I did **not** need change-manager approval, since v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production. Any future attempt to re-deploy v2.3.1 (or a build derived from it) would require change-manager approval, as v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production.
- Root cause of the v2.3.1 regression is still unknown — rollback restored service but didn't address why the release broke health checks.
